chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who had intercourse with his wife and had not shortened (his hair, nails, etc.), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should sacrifice a camel, and I fear that his Hajj has been broken if he was knowledgeable (of the ruling), but if he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: One performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Mu'tamir who has intercourse with his wife before shortening his hair for Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the penalty for a Mu'tamir who engages in marital relations before performing Qasr, prescribing the sacrifice of a camel. The Imam’s hesitation regarding the validity of the Hajj ('Thulima') highlights the scholarly nuance between the nullification of the ritual itself versus the obligation of the penalty, distinguishing between the knowledgeable who are held to a higher standard and the ignorant who may be exempt from further penalty. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on intent and knowledge in determining the severity of ritual breaches during Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the performer of Tumatto falling upon his wife, and he had not shortened (hair, nails, etc.). So heasws said: ‘He should sacrifice a camel, and Iasws am fearful that he has broken his Hajj if he was knowledgeable (of it), but if he did not know, so there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) and performs sexual intercourse with his wife before Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on).
He (the Imam) said, ‘He must slaughter one Jazur and I fear for his al-Hajj to have become damaged if he did knowingly; but if he is ignorant, he is not obligated for anything in this matter.’”
